newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Aer Lingus strike averted after last-ditch talks.
newsitem.headline: Aer Lingus strike averted after last-ditch talks.

text.p: A threatened strike by pilots at Irish national carrier Aer Lingus was averted on Sunday with only hours to spare when both sides agreed a compromise package after last-ditch talks to settle the dispute.
Aer Lingus and the Irish Airline Pilots' Association (IALPA) accepted proposals drawn up by Ireland's Labour Court after two days of talks.

Pilots had threatened to strike from midnight in protest at Aer Lingus' rejection of a 17 percent pay rise recommended by an independent tribunal. Aer Lingus said it would have been bankrupted by the pay award.

The Labour Court recommended that Aer Lingus grant pilots a five percent pay rise from October, and said an independent expert should be appointed to determine whether it was financially viable to pay them the full 17 percent.
"Aer Lingus will be accepting the Labour Court recommendation in its entirety," said Gary McGann, group chief executive at Aer Lingus.
"We're particularly pleased to see that the viability of the company is recognised as being paramount," he told Irish television.
Aer Lingus recently emerged from a major restructuring programme aimed at ensuring its survival after years of heavy losses.
It said acceptance of the pilots' demand could have prompted calls for similar pay rises from other staff and bankrupted the company within a few years.
But pilots argued that their 17 percent pay claim had been recommended by an independent tribunal and should be honoured.

Aer Lingus made a pre-tax profit of 17.8 million punts ($28.51 million) in 1995, its first profit for several years, following the restructuring plan which saw the Irish government give the airline 175 million punts over a three-year period.
In return, the airline cut costs by shedding 1,530 jobs or 12 percent of the workforce and by disposing of non-core assets such as its hotel chain.
